maria.chen: Seeing a spike of 413s from the embeddings endpoint when customers send large batches (dims=768). Started around 09:12 UTC. Anyone touch quotas or ingress limits? Logs: https://logs.internal/abcd1234 :thinking:
kevin: We didn't change global quotas yesterday. Is this tenant-specific or all customers? Can you paste a sample request body?
maria.chen: Example payload (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-768",
  "input": [[0.1,0.2,...], [0.3,0.4,...], ...]  // ~420 vectors, dims=768
}
```
sanjay: Ingress currently enforces two hard checks: max_payload_bytes=1_600_000 and max_vectors_per_request=512. If the JSON byte length > limit we return 413 payload_too_large. Also we validate dims per-vector early and return 400 if a chunk has wrong shape.
olivia: FWIW some clients are sending newline-separated arrays which increases bytes. Also kernel selection is sensitive to batch shapes — mixing very large and tiny batches triggers a slow code path.
kevin: On routing: embeddings requests get routed to emb-pool by route policy (route=embeddings, weight=1.0). The ingress used to split large batches into sub-batches to fit pool batch_capacity, but there's a bug where the splitter wasn't preserving dims metadata and the worker rejects with 400. That would explain 413/400 mix.
maria.chen: Ah ok that matches traces — some requests saw a 413, others 400 after split. Customers hitting this are on Dedicated and Hosted.
sanjay: Proposed immediate fixes: 1) tighten validation to return 413 before we attempt split so clients see a consistent error, 2) fix splitter to keep dims header, 3) emit metrics for any split event so we can track. I'll put up a PR.
kevin: Agree. Long-term we should consider relaxing payload_bytes by allowing binary-encoded vectors (msgpack or base64) to reduce JSON overhead. But that is an API change.
olivia: API debate: do we accept mixed input types? or require canonical JSON array-of-arrays. Also adding a request flag that controls splitting semantics would be useful: e.g., "x-emb-split: error|split" so clients can opt-in.
maria.chen: Console/Docs ask: can we show per-route effective limits and an estimate of cost per 1k embeds? Customers keep assuming they can send arbitrarily large batches.
kevin: We can add two console bits: (1) per-route quota/limits display (payload bytes, vectors/request, dims accepted), (2) cost estimator that takes vectors and returns approximate token/compute cost. For rollout, do the ingestion fix behind a feature flag, canary 1% then 10% then 100%.
sanjay: Telemetry additions: emit metrics emb.request_vectors, emb.request_bytes, emb.split_count, emb.split_size_histogram, and a tag for dims/model. That will let dashboards show p50/p95 latency vs payload size. I'll add statsd counters + tracing span for splitter.
kevin: Minor naming note: use metric prefix redwood.embeddings.* to keep consistent. Also add an alert on split_rate > 0.5% for high failure risk.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Started canary deploy of "fix/ingress-split-dims" to emb-ingress-canary (1%) at commit abc123 :rocket:
maria.chen: Great — I'll update the public docs + internal runbook (PR #456) and ping support to watch for related tickets. Thanks! :thumbsup:
